requirements.title: Role and combinational behavior
requirements.description: The module is a stateless 64-bit adder/subtractor. It has no clock, reset, enable, handshake, stored operands or backpressure. Both outputs respond to the current inputs after combinational settling, independently of earlier inputs.

requirements.title: Native interface and bit order
requirements.description: Inputs are `alu_cmd[0:3]`, `fxu_areg_q[0:63]`, `fxu_breg_q[0:63]` and scalar `local_error_found`. Outputs are `bin_sum[0:63]` and scalar `bin_ovfl`. Index 0 is the most significant bit; index 63 is the least significant bit. Ports carry unsigned bit vectors; signed overflow interprets the same operand bits as two's-complement signed integers. There are no parameters.

requirements.title: Command selection
requirements.description: Command 0010 selects subtraction. Command 0001 selects addition. All other fully known 4-bit encodings are defined addition aliases with exactly the same data and overflow behavior as 0001. There is no invalid-command response or extra error output. Operand A always uses all 64 bits of `fxu_areg_q`.

requirements.title: Addition and carry
requirements.description: For every non-subtraction command, `bin_sum` is A plus the effective operand B defined in R-CALC-007, modulo 2^64. Carry propagates across every bit and byte boundary throughout the 64-bit word. Unsigned carry out is discarded; there is no saturation.

requirements.title: Subtraction and borrow
requirements.description: For command 0010, `bin_sum` is A minus the original B modulo 2^64. All 64 B bits participate at their corresponding positions, including index 11 independently of indices 0 and 1. This includes the two's-complement increment, so A minus A is zero and zero minus one is all ones. `local_error_found` has no effect on subtraction.

requirements.title: Signed overflow
requirements.description: `bin_ovfl` reports signed overflow of the complete 64-bit operation. Addition overflows when the two effective operands have equal signs and the wrapped result has the opposite sign. Subtraction overflows when original A and B have different signs and the wrapped result's sign differs from A. This is neither unsigned carry/borrow nor low-32-bit overflow. The flag is computed from the same effective operands as the result.

requirements.title: Local error injection
requirements.description: On addition and all addition aliases, `local_error_found=0` leaves B unchanged. When it is 1, effective B starts as the original B, then index 51 takes original B[50] and index 59 takes original B[58]. All other bits remain unchanged. These simultaneous replacements can affect subsequent arithmetic carry; they are not output bit flips. Index 50 has higher numeric weight than index 51, and likewise 58 versus 59. Subtraction bypasses both replacements regardless of the flag.

requirements.title: Outputs and observation window
requirements.description: Both outputs are meaningful for every fully known input combination once combinational propagation has settled. They have no valid signal and no required clock edge. No carry, borrow, zero-detect or internal debug signal is exposed. The result and overflow must belong to the same current operation.

requirements.title: Boundaries and wraparound
requirements.description: The full operand range is supported: zero, all ones, single set/clear bits, alternating patterns and both signed extrema. Carries and borrows cross the low/high 32-bit boundary. Equal operands subtract to zero; zero and all-one operands receive no special saturation or masking. Bit indices use the native ascending ranges throughout.

requirements.title: Four-state and input validity
requirements.description: Arithmetic is specified for known 0/1 operands and known command bits. Inputs may change independently; transient values before settling are not sampled. An X or Z `local_error_found` is irrelevant during subtraction and must not corrupt its defined outputs. For addition, if both affected source/destination pairs are equal known bits, the flag is likewise irrelevant, including X/Z. Otherwise an unknown flag, an unknown operand bit or an unknown command has no guaranteed numeric result; it must not be interpreted as a valid zero-valued operation. Once the inputs return to the defined domain, both outputs recover combinationally without reset.
